clue.text: Paul, lecturer to criminals?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A man named Paul teaches a class of inmates in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The don sits next to the cons, as 'to' suggests. Sir Paul Condon was Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police in the 1990s, so the criminals are apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Condon headed London's Metropolitan Police, a real person whose first name is the definition.

clue.text: Paul verbally quotes a Bronte

indicators.note: verbally means spoken rather than written, so we want the sound of the phrase

parts.note: quotes means says, and Anne is one of the three Bronte sisters

explanation.surface: A man called Paul recites a line from one of the Bronte sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: Says Anne, spoken aloud, gives the surname of the French painter Paul Cezanne.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cezanne was the French post-impressionist painter, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Bottle which transmits message

definitions.meaning: first meaning: courage, as in British slang 'to lose your bottle'

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase: the thing which transmits a message
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fibre in the body carrying signals to and from the brain

explanation.surface: A message in a bottle drifting across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The message in a bottle picture hides British slang: bottle means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and a signal-carrying fibre in the body share one word, both everyday senses.

clue.text: None stood around and no one stood around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being turned about and moved into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters used as written

explanation.surface: Two halves of a riddle about nobody standing anywhere nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The same words play two roles: the first 'around' rearranges letters, the second describes the lonely scene. On one's tod is British rhyming slang (Tod Sloan, alone).
explanation.definitionFit: If nobody is standing about you, you are entirely alone, which is what the British slang phrase means.

clue.text: Paul, royally attired?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Paul, the American bass singer and actor

definitions.note: a description: dressed in regal garments
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split into two words, wearing the robes of a monarch

explanation.surface: A man called Paul dressed up like a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the surname as ROBES ON and it describes someone in regal dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was the American singer of Ol' Man River, so his first name points to him.

clue.text: Discovers deep resonant sounds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: finds out a secret or scheme, British informal
second meaning: low rolling noises like thunder

explanation.surface: Someone detects low booming noises.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal use, to find out someone's deceit is to rumble them; the noun means low rolling thunder-like noises.

clue.text: Sweet sweaty smell given honour

parts.note: BO is body odour
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A smelly, sweaty person is awarded an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective describing the smell, but it is the noun, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a frozen dome-shaped dessert, and in British English a sweet is any pudding course.

clue.text: Lest a sin's done without it?

indicators.note: done can mean done over or ruined, so these letters are knocked into new order

parts.note: the nine letters used as written

explanation.surface: A moral warning: avoid sinning, so you stay pure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' is the stain that a sin would leave, so the whole clue hints at a soul kept spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stainless is free of marks or blemishes, so without a stain, the 'it' meant here.

clue.text: Paul, domestically enlightened?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Paul, the American film star

definitions.note: a description of a modern man who shares the housework
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a 1980s British term for a man who does his share of chores and childcare

explanation.surface: A man named Paul who has learned to help around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'new man' was a 1980s British media label for a caring, housework-sharing modern male.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Newman was the Hollywood actor of Butch Cassidy, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Consternation at sweet potatoes I'd brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up turns it to read from bottom to top

parts.note: yams are sweet potatoes in American usage
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is alarmed by the sweet potatoes they have just vomited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' plays on being sick, but in a down clue it sends the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay and consternation are synonyms for sudden alarm and distress.

clue.text: An element of ruin, 'coz I'm reckless

indicators.note: reckless behaviour is wild and careless, so the letters are flung about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring apostrophes

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their own ruin by admitting their reckless nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Zirconium is a metallic chemical element, number 40 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Catcall of Woody Allen's ex losing distant right

indicators.note: losing means the name must give up some of its letters

parts.note: the actress Mia Farrow was Woody Allen's partner
far means distant
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Jeering at Woody Allen's former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catcall' suggests a jeer at the actress, but it is literally a cat's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a cat makes is a miaow, the British spelling of meow, so it is a cat's call.

clue.text: Pleasant accommodating Oriental relative

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to a guest, so one word holds the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant
E is the abbreviation for east, and oriental means eastern

explanation.surface: A friendly relative who puts up a guest from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of a sibling.

clue.text: All 9 I refined after many, many years

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

indicators.note: refined material has been reworked and processed, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
the number spelt out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cryptic sum: all nine, plus one, polished up over a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the rearranged letters behind the M. The 9 is a number to spell out, not a reference to 9-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are periods of a thousand years each, so the plural means a very long stretch of time.

clue.text: Karaoke's ultimate "My Way" bound to show emo-tional understanding

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of karaoke

indicators.note: bound means tied round, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: taken as written
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Singing the closing number, My Way, at karaoke is sure to show deep feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'emo-tional' winks at emo music, keeping the karaoke picture going.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the ability to share and understand another person's feelings.

clue.text: The first moral we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so we go by sound

parts.note: a moral is an ethical rule or standard of conduct

explanation.surface: A storyteller announces the first lesson of the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words differ in spelling only: the rule ends -ple, the chief ends -pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal is the chief or foremost one, the person or thing ranking first.

clue.text: This should be comfortable for the solver?

definitions.text: This should be comfortable for the solver?

parts.note: surface reading: a cosy piece of furniture you sit on
setter's reading: the setter sets the puzzle, so the solver is the one who is set, a playful coinage

explanation.surface: A setter hopes the solver finds this puzzle easy going.
explanation.walkthrough: If the person who sets is the setter, the person set to is, by the same -ee pattern as employee, the settee.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, an upholstered seat for two or more, which ought to be comfortable.

clue.text: Expression of sympathy yelled on course, thus

parts.note: 'there, there' is said to comfort someone
golfers shout fore on the golf course to warn of a ball in flight

explanation.surface: Someone shouts consolation on a golf course after a bad shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and thus are synonyms meaning as a result or consequently.

clue.text: Toothy comedian?

definitions.note: an adjective pointing to a kind of tooth, not a synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the back molar that often arrives late in adulthood
second meaning: Norman, the British slapstick comic actor

explanation.surface: A comedian with a big toothy grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Norman Wisdom was a much-loved British film comedian of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: The last molars are named after this quality, and the comic actor Norman bore it as his surname.

clue.text: Copes with the reason for our mortality?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: handles or deals with something

definitions.note: a phrase to be read as two words: humanity grows old
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split in two, mankind grows older, which is why we die

explanation.surface: Someone deals with the knowledge that we must all die.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as MAN AGES to read the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a problem is to cope with or handle it successfully.

clue.text: Worthy of reverence, as no longer so lazy?

definitions.note: a playful description, read as a bed with less in it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: LESS placed inside BED, someone who spends less time in bed

explanation.surface: A reformed idler is now held in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as B(LESS)ED: less in bed, so less of a sluggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blessed is holy or sacred, deserving veneration.

clue.text: Lout upset with his problems as a youth

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means turned upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout or hooligan

indicators.note: problems suggests trouble and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hooligan troubled by his adolescent difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means like a young lad, behaving in a youthful way.

clue.text: Paul leads in trickery?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Paul, the British television magician

definitions.note: a description of a top magician
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a description of the man himself, a leading conjuror

explanation.surface: A man called Paul is the best at deception.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Daniels was a hugely popular British TV magician of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician's first name picks him out, and conjuring tricks were his whole career.

clue.text: Paul's friend, a horny beast?

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so 'Paul is' becomes I'm
a pal is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter's friend is a randy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter's pen name, so 'Paul's' means the setter is, which he would say as I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, and the males carry long ridged horns.

clue.text: Lords are poetical, longing over Paul

parts.note: the Marylebone Cricket Club owns Lord's, the London cricket ground
art is the old poetic form of are, as in thou art

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: Peers in the House of Lords wax lyrical, pining for a man called Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords' suggests peers, but it is the cricket ground, home of the MCC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Paul McCartney is the former Beatle, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Governed as sporting union governed

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union
led means governed or directed

explanation.surface: A sports body is described as having been in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled and governed are synonyms for exercising authority over a country or people.

clue.text: The Spanish and French end could be spritely?

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
fin is French for end

explanation.surface: A European ending that might be lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spritely' is not sprightly; it means like a sprite, a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, small and delicate, as a fairy or sprite would be.

clue.text: Dickens character portrayed as Andy Capp?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the leader of the boy pickpockets in Oliver Twist

definitions.note: a description: with a cigarette in
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Andy Capp, a British comic-strip layabout

explanation.surface: Casting a Dickens role in the style of a newspaper cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the name as FAG IN; fag is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the villainous fence who trains young thieves in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Shock one of me out loud

indicators.note: out loud means spoken, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: the setter is Paul, so one of him is a Paul

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to hear a copy of themselves speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the setter, who signs himself Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, a strong synonym for shock as a verb.

clue.text: Paul needs case — going abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, scattered widely, so the letters move

parts.note: the nine letters used as written

explanation.surface: Paul needs a suitcase because he is going overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Gascoigne, known as Gazza, was an England footballer who famously played in Italy, hence going abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Gascoigne is the English footballer, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Implies everyone used gets abused

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or knocked about, so these letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cynic's claim that anyone exploited ends up mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to refer indirectly or hint, so alludes and implies both mean suggests.

clue.text: First service and where not to put it when returned suggests this game

indicators.note: a returned ball goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of service
a serve should not go into the net

explanation.surface: Advice on serving: keep it out of the net, and you'll recognise the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Service, net and returned all keep the court in view while doing wordplay jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is the racket sport in which a ball is served and returned over a net.
